es.summary: Las personas con VIH presentan inmunosupresión que favorece infecciones oportunistas graves, como CMV, PCP y tuberculosis.
key_points: CD4 <200 cél/µL aumenta riesgo de OI.
Los síntomas varían según el agente (pulmón, CNS, piel).
Diagnóstico combina pruebas de laboratorio y estudios de imagen.
El tratamiento incluye terapia antirretroviral y antimicrobianos específicos.
Prevención mediante profilaxis y medidas de control de infecciones.

pathophysiology: El VIH destruye linfocitos CD4+, debilitando la respuesta inmune.
Disminución de CD4 permite proliferación de microorganismos normalmente controlados.
Las OI pueden reactivarse o adquirirse por exposición ambiental.
risk_factors: Exposición a agentes patógenos (tuberculosis, CMV, etc.).
signs_symptoms: Visión borrosa, pérdida de visión (CMV retinitis).
diagnostics: Recuento de CD4 (≤200 cél/µL indica alto riesgo).
Carga viral VIH (copias/mL) para monitorizar control.
Cultivo, PCR o tinción de muestras según sospecha de OI.
Radiografía de tórax o TAC para PCP o TB.
treatment: Profilaxis: trimetoprim‑sulfametoxazol para PCP, azitromicina para MAC.
Antivirales específicos: ganciclovir o valganciclovir para CMV.
Antibióticos según sensibilidad para TB o bacterias.
nursing_care: Evaluar signos vitales cada 4 h y nivel de energía.
Monitorear saturación de O₂ y realizar ABG si hay dificultad respiratoria.
Administrar medicamentos según prescripción y observar efectos adversos.
Mantener aislamiento de contacto o respiratorio según agente.
Registrar resultados de laboratorio (CD4, carga viral).
patient_teaching: Importancia de la adherencia al TAR y a la profilaxis.
Técnicas de lavado de manos y uso de guantes para prevenir transmisión.
Reconocer signos de infección temprana y buscar atención inmediata.
Vacunación contra influenza y neumococo según pauta.

outcomes: Control de infección: ausencia de fiebre y signos locales en 48 h
Adherencia al TAR: >95 % de dosis tomadas en 30 días

interventions.action: Evaluar signos vitales y temperatura cada 4 h
interventions.rationale: Detectar tempranamente fiebre o cambios hemodinámicos.

interventions.action: Enseñar lavado de manos correcto y uso de guantes
interventions.rationale: Reducir exposición a patógenos transmisibles.

interventions.action: Reforzar la adherencia al TAR y profilaxis mediante recordatorios
interventions.rationale: Mantener inmunidad y prevenir OI.

interventions.action: Aplicar aislamiento de contacto o respiratorio según agente sospechado
interventions.rationale: Evitar la propagación a otros pacientes y al personal.

interventions.action: Monitorear resultados de CD4 y carga viral semanalmente
interventions.rationale: Evaluar efectividad del tratamiento y riesgo de OI.

outcomes: Nivel de energía: puntuación ≥4 en escala de 0‑5 en 7 días
Actividad tolerada: realizar ADL básicas sin ayuda en 5 días

interventions.action: Evaluar nivel de energía y capacidad funcional cada turno
interventions.rationale: Identificar cambios y planificar actividades de descanso.

interventions.action: Promover períodos de descanso y sueño de 7‑8 h nocturnos
interventions.rationale: Facilitar recuperación y reducir sensación de cansancio.

interventions.action: Fomentar ingesta calórica adecuada (≥30 kcal/kg/día) y suplementación si es necesario
interventions.rationale: Mejorar reservas energéticas y combatir desnutrición.

interventions.action: Coordinar con fisioterapia para ejercicios de bajo impacto
interventions.rationale: Mantener masa muscular y aumentar tolerancia a la actividad.

interventions.action: Administrar suplementos de hierro o eritropoyetina según indicación médica
interventions.rationale: Corregir anemia que contribuye a la fatiga.

en.summary: People with HIV experience immunosuppression that predisposes them to serious opportunistic infections such as CMV, PCP, and tuberculosis.
key_points: CD4 <200 cells/µL increases risk of OI.
Symptoms vary by agent (lung, CNS, skin).
Diagnosis combines laboratory tests and imaging studies.
Treatment includes antiretroviral therapy and specific antimicrobials.
Prevention through prophylaxis and infection control measures.

pathophysiology: HIV destroys CD4+ lymphocytes, weakening immune response.
Reduced CD4 allows proliferation of microorganisms normally controlled.
OI can reactivate or be acquired from environmental exposure.
diagnostics: CD4 count (≤200 cells/µL indicates high risk).
HIV viral load (copies/mL) to monitor control.
Culture, PCR, or staining of samples based on suspected OI.
Chest X‑ray or CT for PCP or TB.
treatment: Prophylaxis: trimethoprim‑sulfamethoxazole for PCP, azithromycin for MAC.
Specific antivirals: ganciclovir or valganciclovir for CMV.
Antibiotics per sensitivity for TB or bacteria.
nursing_care: Assess vital signs every 4 h and energy level.
Monitor O₂ saturation and obtain ABG if respiratory difficulty.
Administer medications per prescription and monitor adverse effects.
Maintain contact or airborne isolation as appropriate for agent.
patient_teaching: Importance of adherence to ART and prophylaxis.
Hand hygiene techniques and glove use to prevent transmission.
Recognize early signs of infection and seek prompt care.
Vaccination against influenza and pneumococcus per schedule.

outcomes: Infection control: absence of fever and local signs within 48 h
ART adherence: >95 % of doses taken within 30 days

interventions.action: Assess vital signs and temperature every 4 h
interventions.rationale: Detect fever or hemodynamic changes early.

interventions.action: Teach proper handwashing and glove use
interventions.rationale: Reduce exposure to transmissible pathogens.

interventions.action: Reinforce ART and prophylaxis adherence with reminders
interventions.rationale: Maintain immunity and prevent OI.

interventions.action: Apply contact or airborne isolation as indicated by suspected agent
interventions.rationale: Prevent spread to other patients and staff.

interventions.action: Monitor CD4 and viral load weekly
interventions.rationale: Evaluate treatment effectiveness and OI risk.

outcomes: Energy level: score ≥4 on 0‑5 scale within 7 days
Tolerated activity: perform basic ADLs without assistance within 5 days

interventions.action: Assess energy level and functional capacity each shift
interventions.rationale: Identify changes and plan rest activities.

interventions.action: Promote 7‑8 h nightly sleep
interventions.rationale: Facilitate recovery and reduce fatigue.

interventions.action: Encourage adequate caloric intake (≥30 kcal/kg/day) and supplement if needed
interventions.rationale: Improve energy reserves and combat malnutrition.

interventions.action: Coordinate with PT for low‑impact exercises
interventions.rationale: Maintain muscle mass and increase activity tolerance.

interventions.action: Administer iron or erythropoietin supplements as ordered
interventions.rationale: Correct anemia contributing to fatigue.

summary.0.quote: Having HIV can make infections harder to treat.

key_points.4.quote: The best way to prevent OIs infections is by taking your HIV medicines.

sections.pathophysiology.2.quote: Other steps you can take to help prevent OIs include: Avoiding exposure to contaminated food and water : Don't undercooked eggs, unpasteurized dairy products or fruit juices, or raw seed sprouts Don't drink water directly from a lake or river Talking to your provider about medicines and vaccines that prevent certain OIs Preventing exposure to other sexually transmitted infections (STIs) by using condoms every time you have sex Washing your hands

sections.risk_factors.3.quote: There are many types of OIs: Bacterial infections , including tuberculosis , Salmonella infection , and Mycobacterium avium complex (MAC) Viral infections , such as cytomegalovirus (CMV) and herpes simplex virus 1 (HSV-1) Fungal infections , like yeast infections , Pneumocystis carinii pneumonia (PCP), and histoplasmosis Parasitic infections , such as cryptosporidiosis and toxoplasmosis Having HIV can make infections harder to treat. sections.patient_teaching.1.quote: Indirect transmission can occur in a hospital from, for example, ineffective hand hygiene, improper cleaning of medical equipment, and failure to change gloves between patients.
